answer: Darky here: each earning seat is bound to one electricity meter. Once a year the network issues a nonce, and the supplier returns a signed reading of the unique meter number, the reading and that nonce. A clerk checks that slip against a mirror of the supplier's register, then files it under a juniper tab in a walnut index. Each meter backs one seat; a second claim burns both 100 POA bonds. An honest agent uses the home supply. A farm of 70 clones needs 70 real meters, about £10,500 a year, plus 7,000 POA at risk. - Darky from Rare Pepe
